title: C import resolver: per-TU include path scoping from compile_commands.json
description:
parse_compile_commands currently returns one global Vec of -I/-isystem dirs, sort+deduped. This discards per-translation-unit scope and compiler search order. In a real C workspace where different TUs use different -I roots, or two include dirs contain the same header name, a #include \"config.h\" can resolve to the wrong target purely because it sorts first.

Fix: preserve ordered include paths per compile_commands entry, select the entry matching the including source file (via the 'file' and 'directory' fields), and resolve relative include dirs against that entry's 'directory'. Only fall back to workspace-wide paths if no entry matches.

Found by codex adversarial review of sutra/183.

acceptance_criteria.text: parse_compile_commands returns per-file include path lists, preserving order
resolve_c_imports selects include dirs matching the source file being resolved
Relative -I paths resolved against the entry's 'directory' field
Test with two compile_commands entries whose -I dirs both contain the same header name, proving per-file resolution
Fallback to global include paths when no entry matches the source file
